summary: Training volume over the last 4 weeks has been very low — only 5 sessions totalling around 6.5 hours — which is well below what's needed for a Half Oceanman 5,000m swim in 26 days. Sleep data is consistently poor (averaging under 6 hours most nights, with several nights under 5 hours) and body battery frequently sits in the 20–50 range, indicating chronic under-recovery that is likely suppressing both training capacity and adaptation. The open-water swim pace of ~28–29 min/km is significantly slower than the 2:30/100m (25:00/km) race target, making swim-specific work the most urgent priority heading into race week.
suggestions: Prioritise sleep above all else this week — body battery data shows sustained low readings (frequently 12–46) driven by consistent 3–5 hour nights; even adding 60–90 minutes of sleep per night will improve adaptation from the sessions you do complete.

The 5,000m swim race target at 2:30/100m requires sustained open-water pace — your recent OW swims averaged ~28:45/km (~2:53/100m), so this week's pool sessions should include longer continuous aerobic blocks (1,000–1,500m unbroken) at 2:30/100m to close that gap before taper week.

Keep the Tuesday tempo run on 8 Sep but cap the continuous effort at 20–25 minutes rather than 30–40 minutes given low body battery (30) and poor recent sleep — quality over duration this close to a race.

The Saturday 110km long ride on 12 Sep is well-timed as a final aerobic stimulus before the Half Oceanman taper, but keep watts firmly in Z2 (128–160W) and cut short if fatigue accumulates — arriving rested at the swim start matters more than ride volume.

After the Half Oceanman swim on 3 Oct, allow 3–5 days of genuine recovery before resuming structured training — a 5km open-water race is a meaningful effort and the Treviso 10K is only 8 days later, so the post-race week must be light.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Tempo run 60 min total: 10 min easy warm-up, 20–25 min continuous at 5:35–5:50/km, 10 min easy cool-down — stop the continuous block early if HR exceeds 170 bpm
proposed_changes.reason: Body battery was only 30 on 7 Sep after poor sleep (230 min) and a 224-min ride the day before; shortening the tempo block reduces injury risk and cumulative fatigue 26 days out from the Half Oceanman swim.

proposed_changes.current_session: 110km long ride @ 128–177W, 240 min, add 3x10 min Z3 blocks if bike-peak week
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 90–100km @ 128–160W (lower half of Z2 only), cap at 210 min — omit Z3 tempo blocks entirely this week
proposed_changes.reason: With the Half Oceanman swim 21 days away and chronic under-recovery visible in sleep and body battery data, keeping this ride strictly in lower Z2 preserves aerobic stimulus without accumulating the fatigue that Z3 blocks would add at this stage.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 14–15km @ 6:30–6:45/km, cap at 100 min — easy conversational effort, no negative-split push
proposed_changes.reason: A full 20km long run the day after a long ride, with the Half Oceanman swim 20 days away, risks excessive leg fatigue and compounds the under-recovery pattern already shown in the wellness data — a shorter run still maintains run-base continuity.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 45km @ 120–140W, cap at 90 min — purely aerobic spin, stop early if fatigue or HR climbs
proposed_changes.reason: At 15 days out from the Half Oceanman the priority is showing up to the swim fresh; trimming this already-adjusted ride by an additional 15–20 min further protects leg freshness without sacrificing aerobic maintenance.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 8–10km @ 6:45–7:00/km, cap at 60 min — flat easy effort, HR ≤ 135 bpm throughout
proposed_changes.reason: 14 days before the Half Oceanman swim, keeping the long run under 60 minutes ensures legs are not carrying residual soreness into the final pre-race taper week.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Easy 30–40 min jog at 7:00+/km, HR ≤ 130 bpm — this is one day after the Half Oceanman swim race and the Treviso 10K is 6 days away; treat this as active recovery only
proposed_changes.reason: Running 21.5km the day after a 5,000m open-water race would severely compromise recovery for the Treviso 10K on 10 Oct — a short easy jog promotes blood flow without adding meaningful fatigue.
